final_answer:
Using the supplied SaPS/PdPS/NoPS labels, PS-Self and PS-Part proteins showed clearly different sequence-composition signatures.

Whole-sequence composition: SaPS proteins were more strongly enriched for low-complexity/disorder-associated residues than PdPS. In the curated benchmark, SaPS was most enriched versus NoPS for G (1.44-fold), P (1.30-fold), Q (1.25-fold), T (1.20-fold), and S (1.20-fold). The human hSaPS set replicated this pattern with P (1.26-fold), G (1.25-fold), Q (1.20-fold), and S (1.16-fold). PdPS enrichment was weaker and shifted toward charged/polar residues: curated PdPS was enriched for Q (1.15-fold), P (1.10-fold), R (1.10-fold), K (1.08-fold), and E (1.08-fold), while hPdPS was enriched for R (1.20-fold), K (1.18-fold), Q (1.15-fold), E (1.15-fold), and P (1.08-fold).

IDR-restricted composition sharpened the difference. SaPS IDRs were enriched for aromatic stickers and low-complexity spacers: curated SaPS IDRs had Y 1.81-fold, F 1.78-fold, G 1.36-fold, Q 1.29-fold, and N 1.23-fold versus NoPS IDRs; hSaPS IDRs had Y 2.60-fold, F 1.43-fold, Q 1.31-fold, and N 1.17-fold. PdPS IDRs showed more Y/R/K-associated signal: curated PdPS IDRs had Y 1.42-fold, R 1.18-fold, G 1.16-fold, Q 1.06-fold, and P 1.06-fold; hPdPS IDRs had Y 1.42-fold, R 1.31-fold, N 1.20-fold, K 1.12-fold, and W 1.11-fold.

IDR architecture also differed. SaPS had longer and denser IDRs than PdPS and NoPS: in the curated set the median IDR length was 151 aa for SaPS, 78.5 aa for PdPS, and 20 aa for NoPS; mean IDR fraction was 0.311, 0.216, and 0.110, respectively. Human labels showed the same ordering: mean IDR fraction was 0.326 for hSaPS, 0.267 for hPdPS, and 0.138 for hNoPS.

Predictor ROC-AUCs, computed separately for each mechanism, showed that all available predictors worked better for SaPS than PdPS. In the curated benchmark, SaPS-vs-NoPS AUCs were PLAAC 0.834, PScore 0.831, and catGRANULE 0.817. PdPS-vs-NoPS AUCs were lower: catGRANULE 0.706, PScore 0.662, and PLAAC 0.644. The human proteome labels replicated this: hSaPS-vs-hNoPS AUCs were PLAAC 0.831, catGRANULE 0.813, and PScore 0.813; hPdPS-vs-hNoPS AUCs were catGRANULE 0.726, PScore 0.689, and PLAAC 0.640.

FuzDrop could not be evaluated because the provided `sequence_prediction_filtered.xlsx` file did not contain a FuzDrop score column. This is a data-availability limitation rather than evidence about FuzDrop performance.

Overall, PS-Self proteins carry stronger intrinsic low-complexity, IDR, and aromatic-sticker features, making them easier for sequence predictors to detect. PS-Part proteins have weaker intrinsic sequence signatures and relatively more charged/basic residue signal, consistent with partner-dependent condensation where interaction partners contribute part of the multivalent phase-separation drive. Predictor scores should be interpreted as propensities, not experimental proof of phase separation.
